surface_forms: cette mystérieuse Mme de Guermantes de mon enfance

appraisal_events.evidence: Tous les châteaux des terres dont elle était duchesse, princesse, vicomtesse, cette dame en fourrures bravant le mauvais temps me semblait les porter avec elle, comme des personnages sculptés au linteau d'un portail... cousine du roi.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator states he has adopted his own imaginative point of view and poetically invests the duchesse, seen crossing the courtyard in plain clothes, with the grandeur of all the castles and titles she holds, against the fact that 'many intelligent people' see her as an ordinary woman.

appraisal_events.evidence: combien il était extraordinaire que chez cette mystérieuse Mme de Guermantes de mon enfance j'allasse uniquement afin d'user d'elle pour une simple commodité pratique, comme on fait du téléphone... et dont on se sert maintenant sans même y penser.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly registers how the once-mysterious duchesse has been reduced, through his own habitual visits for practical errands, to a mere convenience like a telephone, deflating the earlier enchantment.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator's poetic imagination locally elevates her by attaching to her plain appearance the full weight of her titles and lands, in contrast to those who see only an ordinary woman.
The closing telephone comparison shows the narrator's former wonder toward her collapsing into unthinking practical use, a local diminishment of her mystique in his eyes.

ambiguities: The narrator explicitly frames his elevated, castle-and-lineage vision of the duchesse as his own chosen point of view, set against 'many intelligent people' who find her title meaningless; it is unclear whether the narration fully endorses this elevation or presents it as a knowing personal indulgence that the closing telephone image goes on to deflate.
